text:
maria_support: FYI BrightBeam (customer) on dedicated pool ded-eu2-aa12 is hitting intermittent p95 spikes (~3s) and ~10% 429s since ~09:50 UTC. They say it started after we pushed the new kernel/driver patch yesterday. Customer is seeing correlation with other tenants on the same host.

ian_sre: Can you paste a few request IDs and a short log snippet? Need to check whether these 429s are router-level rate limits or backend throttles.

maria_support: Example IDs and tiny log slice below — looks like some requests are getting 429 backend_throttle from node ded-eu2-node-43 and others succeed on same node. Seq lengths vary.

```
[2026-03-17T09:58:08Z] rb-req-20260317-01 model=redwood-1 seq=1024 latency=3200ms status=429 reason=backend_throttle node=ded-eu2-node-43 slice=mig0c
[2026-03-17T09:58:12Z] rb-req-20260317-02 model=redwood-1 seq=512 latency=2800ms status=200 node=ded-eu2-node-43 slice=mig1a
[2026-03-17T09:59:03Z] rb-req-20260317-03 model=redwood-1 seq=2048 latency=4200ms status=429 reason=backend_throttle node=ded-eu2-node-43 slice=mig0c
```

dmitri_infra: Node/ slice pattern suggests mixed MIG partitions on the same physical GPU. Could be SM saturation from a noisy sibling or L3 cache thrash. Any recent packing/placement changes?

autoscale-bot: scale_event: pool=ded-eu2-aa12 action=none reason=fragmented_free_slots threshold=0.85

zara_eng: We recently rolled a packing policy tweak that favors fractional packing for density; that can increase fragmentation so autoscaler may opt not to spawn a whole extra node even under burst.

ian_sre: Repro steps from the customer? Is this high concurrency short requests or long streaming sessions?

maria_support: Customer ran a short stress script — many concurrent short streaming calls. They shared this example: 
```
for i in {1..1000}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & done
wait
```

zara_eng: That pattern hits many small sequences concurrently — good candidate for KV-cache churn and SM time-slicing noise. Autoscaler refusal (fragmented slots) + noisy neighbor could explain 429 bursts when the scheduler temporarily queues requests.

dmitri_infra: Plan proposal: 1) live-migrate BrightBeam off ded-eu2-node-43 to an isolated host to validate (2h window), 2) temporarily relax autoscaler fragmentation threshold for this pool so it can spawn a fresh node under burst, 3) add router-side per-tenant concurrency cap (soft limit) while we monitor.

ian_sre: Also collect perf counters during the migration: SM util, SM active warps, L2 hit rate, PCIe BW, GPU mem allocs, and kernel time. If SM util for sibling stays high while this tenant's SM time drops -> noisy neighbor.

maria_support: Customer agreed to migration and short throttle. They want ETA.

dmitri_infra: I can schedule migration in ~15m. Will force relocate workloads off node ded-eu2-node-43 -> node-iso-07 and pin BrightBeam there for 2h.

autoscale-bot: schedule_migration: pool=ded-eu2-aa12 target=node-iso-07 eta=900s

zara_eng: I'll push a temporary router tweak to limit concurrent streams to 200 for this tenant and open a monitor dashboard for KV-cache evictions and latency.

ian_sre: After migration, run the customer's stress script once more and record logs + perf counters. If 429s disappear and p95 normalizes, it's noisy neighbor. If not, we escalate deeper (driver/kernel).

maria_support: Noted. I'll tell BrightBeam the plan and start the migration window. Thanks team :thumbsup:

ian_sre: One more note — if we confirm noisy neighbor, recommend a medium-term mitigation: add a placement policy for this pool to prefer contiguous MIG slices or reserve 1 whole GPU per node for high-burst tenants. Will draft RFC.

maria_support: Will update customer after migration and paste results here."
